title: He Was Clinically Blind on One Side, Yet Pointed to Lights 90% Right
description:
In 1974 in London, Lawrence Weiskrantz and Elizabeth Warrington discovered 'blindsight': after surgical removal of right primary visual cortex left a young patient consciously blind on his left side, asking him to 'just guess' revealed 90% accuracy pointing to lights and distinguishing shapes via subcortical brainstem and thalamic pathways (Brain, 1974). In 2008, Beatrice de Gelder and colleagues showed that a patient with complete bilateral visual-cortex blindness navigated an obstacle-filled hallway without a cane and with zero collisions.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Weiskrantz L, Warrington EK, Sanders MD, Marshall J (1974) Visual capacity in the hemianopic field following a restricted occipital ablation. Brain 97(4): 709-728. https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/97.1.709
- de Gelder B, Tamietto M, van Boxtel G et al. (2008) Intact navigation skills after bilateral loss of striate cortex. Current Biology 18(24): R1128-R1129. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2008.11.002
